Let's look at artillery and how a howitzer is used. The optimal is 6 men work the gun and a Sargeant. Each man has a specific role at each step of the process. These 6 men do not rotate roles, they might have a good idea of what each role is and be competent to perform if need be; but they have a specific role that never changes. The Sargeant is the supervisor who can fill in at any role at any time for any reason.

But let us think of the chain of command. The generals decide to attack a village. Colonels decide how to attack a village. Majors send the commands to best use the assets. Lieutenants receive the orders and inform the specific units. Specific units carry out the orders (I know this is dumb downed and overly simplified but let's pretend this is exactly how it works -- I'm sure it isn't).
